subject: Performance SLOs & multi-region routing — post-call recap and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finova.com>, Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@finova.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLOs & multi-region routing — post-call recap and next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have aligned next steps. Please confirm or correct any items below.

Summary of requirements (from call):
- Target P95 latency: 200ms for short-form text generation (<=256 tokens) in the US; 250ms target for EU; 300ms target for APAC (streaming support required).
- Throughput: baseline 12k requests/day, expected to peak at ~120 reqs/s during batch windows.
- Concurrency: up to 500 concurrent inference requests across the org; per-user concurrency expected to be <= 50.
- Streaming: partial token streaming required for UI responsiveness (users expect first tokens within ~80-100ms of request start).
- Data residency: production data for EU users must remain in EU regions; APAC traffic must be routed to APAC region only. Customer requires data residency certification and optional BYOK for EU workloads.
- Failover/DR: automatic fallback to a compatible model variant in another region with relaxed latency SLA in case of regional outage.

Open questions we noted:
1) Do you require strict per-customer tenancy (Dedicated) for EU workloads or is region-based isolation sufficient?
2) Any requirements around KMS/HSM (BYOK) for EU data?
3) Expected percent of streaming vs non-streaming requests (ballpark) so we can size streaming-optimized nodes.

Attachments: redwood-slo-draft.pdf (SLO draft), network-requirements.xlsx (network/firewall needs)

Proposed next steps:
- Confirm the open questions above (quick reply) — Alex/Priya
- Technical deep-dive with our solutions engineer (30-45m) — propose Thu 7/22 or Fri 7/23
- Draft SOW/SLA for Dedicated region configuration and data residency options (we will send within 3 business days after deep-dive)

If that looks right I will schedule the deep-dive and loop in Vivek (solutions) and Aditya (account exec).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0143

---

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap — mostly matches our notes. A few clarifications:
- We can accept 250ms P95 for EU as you list; APAC target of 300ms is fine. For some latency-sensitive flows we may want P90 <= 150ms in the US — is that achievable with streaming?
- Streaming: ~30% of requests will be streaming (chat UI), the rest will be non-streaming batch calls.
- Concurrency: peak concurrency of 500 is our upper bound; typical concurrency will be ~120.
- Data residency: EU production data must remain in EU. We prefer region-based isolation with BYOK (we have an EU KMS). Dedicated tenancy is not strictly required unless you flag compliance blockers.

Procurement update: Gina Ross (cc'd) will lead procurement. She requested an early view of the SOW and any references/documents on data residency and KMS integration.

Can do the technical deep-dive Thu 7/22 10-11am ET.

Appreciate it —
Alex
VP Product, Finova
alex.johnson@finova.com
+1 (212) 555-0199

Alex / Priya —

Great — thanks for the clarifications. Confirming the deep-dive: Thu 7/22 10:00-10:45am ET (we'll send a calendar invite).

Quick answers to your questions:
- P90 targets: streaming paths are optimized for low first-byte time; we can target P90 <= 150ms in the US on streaming-optimized nodes assuming the client connection (network) is healthy. We'll validate during the technical deep-dive with a short synthetic test.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: noted ~30% streaming — we'll size initial clusters accordingly and run a capacity simulation during the technical call.
- Data residency & BYOK: we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) in EU regions and can deploy region-scoped Dedicated pools. For clients that need stronger isolation, we can offer Dedicated nodes pinned to the EU region (SLA/price difference applies).

Attachments: I attached the draft SLO and network requirements (redwood-slo-draft.pdf, network-requirements.xlsx). I'll also share a short internal note with Vivek & Aditya to surface routing and deployment options ahead of the call.

Next steps (owner):
- Marissa: send calendar invite + invite Vivek (solutions) and Aditya (account exec) — today
- Vivek: prepare a short routing/infra slide (multi-region options + expected latency profile per-region) — before Thu deep-dive
- Marissa: send initial SOW/SLA draft after the deep-dive (T+3 business days)

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

Best,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Performance SLOs & multi-region routing — post-call recap and next steps

Folks —

Quick internal note ahead of Thu deep-dive. Key options for Finova based on requirements:

1) Region-based Dedicated pools (recommended initial approach)
   - Deploy Dedicated inference pool in us-west-2, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1.
   - Smart routing at the edge routes EU/APAC traffic to respective pools; US traffic hits us-west-2 by default.
   - BYOK: enable customer KMS for EU pool; requires KMS integration during onboarding (doc & runbook).
   - Latency profile (estimate, tuned at 256 tokens): US P95 ~180-220ms; EU P95 ~230-270ms; APAC P95 ~280-320ms.

2) Strict Dedicated for EU only (if procurement requires tenancy)
   - Pin EU customer workload to a Dedicated cluster (higher cost, stronger isolation).

3) Streaming considerations
   - Streaming-optimized nodes with pinned CPU/network path; ensure long-lived connections are routed to streaming clusters.
   - We should validate first-byte times with a synthetic streaming test during the call (I will prepare a small script).

Network/Firewall notes:
- Need customer to allow outbound to our eu-west-1 endpoints and to the S3 buckets used for model artifacts (we will provide CIDR ranges).

Attachments: multi-region-routing.png (infra sketch)

I'll prepare the two-slide routing summary and synthetic test plan before Thu. LMK if we want to propose tight P90 guarantees in the SOW or keep as an aspiration pending validation.

-Vivek
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
